findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The cap arithmetic holds: rent of GBP 1300 a month is GBP 15,600 a year, five weeks of that is GBP 1,500.00, and the stated deposit is GBP 1,500. So the amount is at, not above, the cap, and no breach is shown. The conclusion stays conditional because jurisdiction and tenancy type are unknown in the context. Nothing in the contract confirms the property is in England or that this is an ordinary covered private tenancy. It also does not confirm that the rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The Rent and Tenancy deposit clauses (s5, s6) support the figures but not these scope facts. No quoted counter-evidence defeats the issue. This amount check says nothing about deposit protection or authenticity. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants

questions: Is this a private tenancy in England with the landlord living elsewhere?
What rent period and tenancy does the deposit cover, and can the amount be revised?

expectations.explanation: message_checker:untraceable_payment is a payment_safety finding. It cites the request to buy GBP 1500 in prepaid gift cards and send redemption codes, which is the payment mechanism and not the owner's location.

message_checker:viewing_refused is an in_person_viewing finding. It cites "You cannot view until you pay." and the refusal of any viewing before the codes arrive. message_checker:payment_before_viewing supports it on the payment side.
emotion_classifier:pressure_urgency is a no_pressure finding. It cites the 16 November 18:00 deadline with the threat to give the room to someone else, attached to the gift-card demand.

message_checker:landlord_abroad is filed under in_person_viewing, not landlord_identity. The landlord_identity check stays unverified with no findings, so no false identity or lack of authority is inferred from the owner being abroad. The decision reasons list identity as "Not yet verified".

forbidden_assertions.explanation: The abroad finding is a medium-confidence suspicion flag (hard_flag false). The likely_scam verdict rests on the gift-card demand, payment before viewing and the deadline, not on the owner being abroad alone.

No output claims impersonation because the owner and agent names differ. The outputs record Rowan Pike as the contract's letting representative and do not treat the different names as a contradiction.

The contract finding is explicitly conditional and says the cap check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. The verdict stays likely_scam, so the contract does not cancel the gift-card request.

unsupported_claims.output_quote: £1,300 a month against roughly £950 for a room in W12 (approximate area figure): about 37% higher.
unsupported_claims.explanation: The £950 area benchmark is not in any supplied source and no external record backs it. Its "supports": "suspicious" label also sits oddly with its own info severity and its "Not a scam sign" wording.

grounding_issues.explanation: The quote "£1,300 pcm" matches only a structured rendering of the listing rent. The evidence_id "listing" is not an uploaded evidence item. The £950 comparison figure has no source, so the finding is weakly grounded.

The quote matches the source, but the finding says "The agent asks for money before you have seen the property" while the chat shows the student asking to view before paying. This is mild, because the agent's message does make viewing conditional on payment.

grading.reviewer_note: Decision likely_scam is in the allowed outcomes. The Companies House lookup returned an error (503) and was not treated as evidence either way. Unverified identity and right_to_let are kept as unknown. The message_checker question asks whether the student has seen the flat, but the student asked to view before paying and was refused. That is a minor mismatch and does not affect any expectation.
